kartice.naslov: Coarse-tuning to improve a protein foundation model for a domain of proteins: the example of outer membrane beta barrels
kartice.povzetek_sl: Foundation models for proteins have shown great potential in addressing a wide range of challenges in computational molecular biology. State-of-the-art models are trained on large and diverse corpora of protein sequences, enabled by self-supervised training. The models are then used in transfer learning and the embeddings they calculate are used in supervised downstream tasks. We propose a novel focusing mechanism for foundation models, which we call 'coarse-tuning'. In coarse-tuning, we further update the model, using a defined yet unlabeled, dataset to enhance its performance in a specific domain. We demonstrate this approach using Outer Membrane Beta Barrels (OMBBs) - proteins that are found in the distinct biophysical environment of the outer membrane. Our results show that coarse-tuned models outperform the original foundation model when applied to various transfer learning tasks. kartice.naslov: Self-organized criticality in a mammalian RNA-interference circuit
kartice.povzetek_sl: Living systems have been argued to operate near critical points, but their relevance at the cellular level is poorly understood. Critical states allow for a high sensitivity to external inputs and maximal information transfer and display fluctuations at all scales. Critical points are very special, and require the fine tuning of a control parameter, which is hard to reconcile with the robustness of living cells. Self-organized criticality (SOC) proposes that feedback, rather than tuning, brings a system to its critical point. Here we show that RNA interference, in which messenger RNAs compete for shared silencing machinery and so queue for service, together with negative feedback gives rise to SOC in mammalian cells. In a synthetic circuit, a protein repressor whose mRNA competes with the mRNA of a fluorescent reporter that it represses senses the congestion of the queue, closing the feedback loop. Theory and stochastic simulations show that the loop holds the queue near its critical point despite changes in its parameters, and that expression becomes intermittent, with scale-free bursts. kartice.naslov: Associative Learning and Memory Erasure in a Synthetic Multicellular System
kartice.povzetek_sl: Learning is a basic form of adaptation that organisms display from neural systems to single cells. In associative learning, the pairing of two stimuli lets one of them evoke the response to the other. Engineering this behavior in a living cell is difficult, because coincidence detection, memory, and conditional readout must be wired into a single regulatory network. Here we build a consortium of five E. coli strains that distributes the operations of associative learning and communicates through one diffusible quorum-sensing signal. The same signal acts as the memory trace. One strain detects the coincidence of the two inputs, a second maintains the memory through positive feedback in the shared medium, a third reads it out on the conditioned stimulus, a fourth reports the unconditioned response, and a fifth erases the memory on command. We show experimentally that the assembled consortium learns the association, since a stimulus that is silent before training evokes a strong response after pairing. kartice.naslov: An anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis formulation for the in vitro study of oxygen sensitive proteins
kartice.povzetek_sl: Anaerobic microbes harbor unique enzymes and metabolic pathways with potential biotechnological applications, yet these microbes remain difficult to study and engineer. Research is limited by the labor-intensive workflows required to maintain anoxic environments and the lack of genetic tools available for non-model anaerobes. Here, we present an anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) platform for the in vitro study of oxygen-sensitive enzymes. This study establishes two methods for conducting anaerobic CFPS, achieving an anoxic environment by (1) sparging with inert gas or (2) lyophilizing to remove oxygenated water. We show the functionality of our anaerobic CFPS formulation by producing oxygen-independent fluorescent protein reporters and a [4Fe-4S] cluster pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) with a specific activity of 5.2 {+/-} 0.3 x 10-4 U/{micro}L cell-free extract. This highly modular platform will allow study of diverse oxygen-sensitive proteins and requires only minor modifications to commonly used CFPS workflows.

kartice.povzetek_sl: Plasmacytoid urothelial carcinoma (PUC) is an aggressive histologic subtype of bladder cancer associated with worse patient outcomes and therapeutic response compared to conventional urothelial carcinoma (CUC). While recent work has demonstrated metastatic lymph nodes from PUC tumors have an inflamed phenotype, how the tumor microenvironment (TME) and crosstalk between tumor, stromal, and immune cells in primary PUC bladder tumors differs from those in CUC remains poorly understood. The impact of these differences on response to immunotherapy is also unknown. To understand TME differences between CUC and PUC and their impact on cell signaling, we performed single nucleus RNA sequencing on PUC and CUC tumors, as well as Xenium spatial transcriptomics on a mixed CUC / PUC tumor. kartice.povzetek_sl: Brain functional activity emerges within an underlying structural scaffold. While structural network connectivity provides a relatively stable anatomical backbone for large-scale communication, functional interactions are high-dimensional and temporally dynamic, forming recurrent patterns that can be represented in a latent space of transient functional states. Yet, how these transient functional states are organized and the extent to which they remain constrained by structural network connectivity or become relatively decoupled from structural organization over time remain poorly understood. kartice.naslov: Selected for the surface: adaptive laboratory evolution for accelerated cathodic biofilm development in Cupriavidus necator
kartice.povzetek_sl: Cupriavidus necator is a metabolically versatile facultative chemolithoautotroph and a promising chassis for sustainable bioproduction from CO2. Efficient coupling of its metabolism to renewable electricity through microbial electrosynthesis (MES) requires the organism to form stable, electroactive biofilms on cathodes. This step is hindered under oxic conditions (oxic MES, oMES) by electrochemically generated reactive oxygen species (ROS), mass-transfer limitations and poor biofilm stability. Systematic strategies to improve C. necator biofilm formation on cathodes have been lacking. Here we used adaptive laboratory evolution (ALE) to address this gap. The progenitor strain colonised graphite cathodes only after an initial heterotrophic phase and formed spatially uneven biofilms whose distribution mirrored the local flow field, as resolved by micro-particle tracking velocimetry. kartice.povzetek_sl: Loss of skeletal muscle strength and mobility is among the most consequential features of human aging, yet the molecular programs that accompany this decline in women remain poorly understood. Here, we performed deep comprehensive data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomic profiling of vastus lateralis biopsies from 10 younger (24-30 years) and 10 older (70-84 years) healthy women enrolled through the NIH Common Fund Cellular Senescence Network (SenNet), with matched measurements of grip strength and gait speed. Of 2,391 quantified protein groups, 163 were significantly altered with age, and partial least squares-discriminant analysis completely separated the age groups (cross-validated AUC = 1.00).
